summary: Three unrelated areas: CIP-19 addresses (scalus-core), CIP-57 blueprints (scalus-core) and the BIP-39/BIP32-Ed25519/CIP-1852 HD wallet (scalus-cardano-ledger). The cluster is cheap (about 1.5 s; the only cost is repeated PBKDF2 in the HD suites, C35-15). Pointer and variable-length decoding are tested thoroughly against the ledger; the rest of CardanoAddressTest is example-based, with many repeated type-id/header/Byron asserts and a few that cannot fail, and no property uses the cluster's own address generator. Reading the main code against cardano-ledger found four main-code defects: Address.fromBytes and TransactionOutput accept addresses the ledger's decodeAddr rejects (C35-1, pinned by the TransactionOutput generator, C35-9), the blueprint Purpose codec cannot round-trip OneOf (C35-2), Bip39 skips NFKD normalization (C35-3), and Cip1852.parsePath accepts negative indices (C35-4). The HD tests have strong oracles (cardano-addresses vector, bloxbean parity) next to many size-only and determinism tests that cannot fail.

findings.claim: By reading, Address.fromBytes claims to be 'the ledger's decodeAddr' (1218-1219) but accepts bytes that decodeAddr rejects. cardano-ledger conway-1.22.1.0, Cardano/Ledger/Address.hs: a Byron address needs header exactly 0x82 (headerByron, 540-544) and is decoded in full with decodeCrcProtected (decodeBootstrapAddress, 688-697; Byron Address.hs:174); a Shelley header must have header .&. 0x8E == 0 (headerNonShelleyBits, 547-548, check at 653-659), so the network nibble is 0 or 1 and types 8-15 are not output addresses. Scalus: (a) any header 0x80-0x8F becomes a ByronAddress with no CBOR or CRC check (1262, 1462-1467), so Address.fromBytes(Array(0x80.toByte)) succeeds and fails only later in the lazy `parsed`; (b) a Shelley header with network nibble 2-15 parses to Network.Other (1317 and the other parseTypeN); (c) TransactionOutput reads its address with Address.read (TransactionOutput.scala:273, 293), so a stake address (header 0xe_/0xf_) is accepted as an output address. A grep of scalus.cardano.ledger.rules finds no rule that references StakeAddress, so such an output passes validation in Scalus and fails deserialization on a node. The tests pin the lax behavior: Arbitrary[TransactionOutput] = autoDerived (ledger ArbitraryInstances:335) draws Address from address.ArbitraryInstances, which yields StakeAddress in 34 % and Network.Other in ~20 % of samples (gen-stats.md), and CborSerializationTest:113 round-trips them.
findings.action: Main-code note: in fromBytes require header == 0x82 for Byron and decode it (reuse ParsedByronAddress.parse + isValid), and reject a Shelley/stake header whose network nibble is not 0 or 1; in TransactionOutput read the address with a variant that rejects StakeAddress (fromBech32("stake1...") must keep returning StakeAddress, RewardAccount.scala:60 relies on it). Tests: add the three negative cases to CardanoAddressTest and a TransactionOutput decode test; then apply C35-9 to the generator.
findings.coverageRisk: none: adds coverage only
findings.verification: The ledger source (../cardano-ledger at conway-1.22.1.0, libs/cardano-ledger-core/src/Cardano/Ledger/Address.hs) matches the claim. headerByron = 0b10000010, and isByronAddress is equality. Byron bytes go through decodeBootstrapAddress -> decodeFull' (lines 688-697). A Shelley header must satisfy header .&. (0x82 .|. 0x0C) == 0 (lines 547-548 and 653-659), so the network is only bit 0 and every header with bit 7 set (types 8-15, stake 0xE_/0xF_) is rejected. Scalus Address.scala:1244-1267 dispatches on the high nibble only. parseType8 (1462-1467) wraps any 0x8_ header in ByronAddress with no CBOR or CRC check; parsed is lazy (928). Network.fromNetworkId (154-157) maps 2-15 to Other. TransactionOutput.scala:273/293 use Address.read (Address.scala:1197-1201), which calls fromBytes, so a StakeAddress is accepted as an output address. In rules/, only WrongNetworkValidator checks output addresses, through getNetwork.contains(expected). A StakeAddress on the right network passes it, so (c) is reachable. Note: WrongNetworkValidator does reject Network.Other at validation, so (b) is a parse-level leniency only, not a validation hole. The generator pins hold: ledger ArbitraryInstances:335 is autoDerived, address ArbitraryInstances:9-17 gives Other at weight 1/5, and CborSerializationTest:112-113 round-trips TransactionOutput.

findings.claim: By reading (lines 485-501 never executed in the baseline): the Purpose JSON codec is incomplete (marked todo in the source). (1) Purpose.OneOf encodes as an empty JSON array `[]`, while CIP-57 writes `{"oneOf": [...]}`; (2) decodeValue calls readString, so it cannot read back the `[]` it wrote, nor the CIP-57 oneOf object that Aiken emits; a blueprint whose TypeDescription has purpose = Some(OneOf(...)) does not round-trip; (3) an unknown purpose string (e.g. "vote" or "propose") falls through the match and throws scala.MatchError instead of in.decodeError. The string "oneOf" decodes to OneOf(Seq.empty).
findings.action: Main-code note: encode OneOf as {"oneOf": [..]} and decode both forms, with decodeError on unknown input. Test: in BlueprintTest, round-trip a TypeDescription for each Purpose case including OneOf(Seq(Spend, Mint)), parse a CIP-57 oneOf object, and assert a decode error (JsonReaderException) for an unknown purpose string.
findings.coverageRisk: none: adds coverage only
findings.verification: Blueprint.scala:482-490: decodeValue calls in.readString and then does a non-exhaustive String match, so an unknown string throws scala.MatchError, not decodeError. "oneOf" maps to OneOf(Seq.empty) with a // todo. Lines 492-501: OneOf encodes as an empty array via writeArrayStart/writeArrayEnd. readString cannot read an array or an object back, so TypeDescription(purpose = Some(OneOf(...))) (411-416, JsonCodecMaker.make) does not round-trip. Compare DataType's codec (459-464), which uses in.decodeError correctly.

findings.claim: By reading: BIP-39 derives the seed with PBKDF2 over the mnemonic 'in UTF-8 NFKD' and salt 'mnemonic' + passphrase 'again in UTF-8 NFKD'. mnemonicToSeed uses passphrase.getBytes("UTF-8") with no NFKD, so a non-ASCII passphrase in composed form (e.g. "caf\u00e9") gives a seed different from other BIP-39 implementations (which decompose to "cafe\u0301"). normalizeWords also uses the default-locale toLowerCase, so on a JVM with a Turkish default locale an upper-case word with I (e.g. "LIBRARY") lowers to a dotless i and the mnemonic is rejected. Cardano keys (Bip32Ed25519.masterKeyFromEntropy) do not use mnemonicToSeed, so the impact is limited to callers of the BIP-39 seed.
findings.action: Main-code note only: NFKD-normalize mnemonic and passphrase (java.text.Normalizer is not available on Scala.js; it needs a platform shim or a documented ASCII-only restriction) and use toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT). Test: add the trezor vectors with a non-ASCII passphrase (the Japanese vector file) on JVM.
findings.coverageRisk: none: adds coverage only
findings.verification: Both defects are real. Bip39.scala:108-113 builds the salt as ("mnemonic" + passphrase).getBytes("UTF-8") with no NFKD. Bip39.scala:201-202 normalizeWords uses the default-locale toLowerCase, so a JVM in a tr locale lowercases "LIBRARY" to a dotless i and the word lookup fails. Scala.js toLowerCase is locale-independent, so this is JVM-only. The impact statement is wrong for the locale part. normalizeWords is also used by mnemonicToEntropy (Bip39.scala:47-48) and isValidMnemonic (23-24). mnemonicToEntropy feeds Bip32Ed25519.masterKeyFromMnemonic (181-183), which HdAccount/HdKeyPair.fromMnemonic use. Corrected claim: the NFKD gap affects only mnemonicToSeed callers, but the locale bug also rejects upper-case mnemonics in the Cardano key path (masterKeyFromMnemonic) on a Turkish-locale JVM. Fix both with Locale.ROOT, and add an upper-case mnemonic test.

findings.claim: By reading: Cip1852.parsePath accepts invalid paths and disagrees with Bip32Ed25519.parsePath. "m/1852'/1815'/0'/0/-1" returns Some((0, 0, -1)) and "m/1852'/1815'/-5'/0/0" returns account -5, because role/index use "-1".toInt and parseHardenedIndex does not check the sign, while Cip1852.path rejects negatives (146-148). parseHardenedIndex accepts ' and H but not h, which Bip32Ed25519.parsePath accepts (229-230); a path without the m/ prefix is accepted (161), while Bip32Ed25519 requires m/ or M/ (218-221) and Cip1852 rejects M/. Low impact: the result is only used to describe a path.
findings.action: Main-code note: reject negative numbers and accept the same suffixes and prefixes as Bip32Ed25519.parsePath. Test: extend Cip1852Test 'parsePath - invalid paths' (71-80) with "-1" role/index/account, a non-hardened purpose "m/1852/1815'/0'/0/0" (reaches the NonFatal catch at 175-177) and the h suffix.
findings.coverageRisk: none: adds coverage only
findings.verification: Cip1852.scala:159-178: role and index use plain toInt, so "-1" and "+1" parse. parseHardenedIndex (204-209) checks only the suffix (' or H) and then toInt, so "-5'" gives account -5. The m/ prefix is optional (161), and "M/..." splits into 6 parts and returns None. Bip32Ed25519.parsePath (216-246) requires m/ or M/, accepts h, and rejects negatives. Cip1852.path (145-149) rejects negatives, so the two disagree. grep finds no use of Cip1852.parsePath or parseAccountPath in main code, so the impact is low (public API only).

findings.claim: No property test in the cluster uses address.ArbitraryInstances, its own generator file. CborSerializationTest:113 already round-trips Address.fromBytes(toBytes) indirectly through TransactionOutput, but no property checks bech32, Byron base58, or the Byron network magic. The examples 'Address serialization' (210-223), 'Address parsing should handle all address types' (225-251), 'Address round-trip' (273-284) and the Byron round trips (618-630, 758-775) are instances of one round-trip law over a single hand-built address. The Byron generator (21-31) produces network-magic attributes, which would reach parseNetworkMagic (874-894, fully uncovered).
findings.action: Add to CardanoAddressTest (with ScalaCheckPropertyChecks and address.ArbitraryInstances): forAll (a: Address) Address.fromBytes(a.toBytes.bytes) == a and a.typeId == header nibble; for Shelley/Stake with network Testnet or Mainnet Address.fromBech32(a.toBech32.get) == a; for ByronAddress ByronAddress.fromBase58(b.toBase58).get == b, b.getNetwork == (if b.networkMagic.isEmpty then Mainnet else Testnet) and b.networkMagic equals the generated magic. Delete 225-251, 273-284, 625-630 and 758-775; keep the CIP-19 vectors (43-48) and the header pins (185-208).
findings.coverageRisk: low: the deleted examples use one fixed hash pair; the property draws all types and networks; Byron equality on the parsed fields (758-775) is implied by equal bytes
findings.verification: The laws hold for every generated input. Shelley/Stake toHeader writes the Other(v) nibble, and fromBytes maps it back to Other(v) (Address.scala:154-157). The Pointer generator stays within the widths. Byron typeId 0x08 matches header 0x82. ByronAddress.create (1046+) CBOR-encodes magics 764824073, 1097911063 and 1, which parseNetworkMagic (874-894) decodes via additional=26 or <24. getNetwork (942-945) gives Testnet for any present magic, which matches the proposed law. The proposed deletions lose one assertion. CardanoAddressTest:625-630 is the only test of ByronAddress.encode (grep finds no other .encode assertion on addresses), and the property does not assert encode. The generator also never produces a derivation path, unlike the Daedalus vector, but 758-775 is implied by the kept 618-623. 225-251 and 273-284 are covered by the round-trip plus the kept header pins (185-208). Corrected action: add b.encode == Success(b.toBase58) to the Byron property, or delete 625-630 only together with C35-7, whose table keeps encode. The Network.Other part of the property must change if the C35-1 fix lands.

findings.verification: The duplicates are real. typeId 0x00 is asserted at 168/238/vector 0, 0x0e at 200/250/vector 14, header 0x01 at 192/217, header 0xe1 at 203/222, and isEnterprise at 182/300. findings.claim: The 14 Byron tests each loop over the same three addresses and call ByronAddress.fromBase58(base58).get again. 'should encode to Base58' (618-623) and 'round-trip through encode' (625-630) assert the same thing because encode == Success(toBase58) (Address.scala:954); 'round-trip preserves all data' (758-775) follows from 618-623; keyHashOption size 28 (642-649) repeats parsed.addrRoot size 28 (681); addrType is asserted as '0 or 2' (683-686) and exactly (727-744).
findings.action: Replace 609-775 with one table: (base58, addrType, hasDerivationPath, attributesSize == 0) for the Icarus, Daedalus and Redeem vectors, and assert in one test: fromBase58 succeeds, typeId 0x08, toBase58 == base58, encode == Success(base58), getNetwork == Mainnet, keyHashOption == Some(AddrKeyHash(parsed.addrRoot)), addrRoot size 28, parsed.isValid, byronAddrType, derivationPath presence, Address.fromString is a ByronAddress, plus hasScript/isEnterprise/scriptHashOption/hrp. Keep the CRC corruption test (659-667) separate.
findings.coverageRisk: none: the table keeps every value assertion; only repeats and the always-true checks of C35-7 go
findings.verification:
Each assertion in CardanoAddressTest:609-775 maps to the proposed table, which uses the same entry point and the same three real vectors, and on all vectors where the old tests used only .head:
- decode success and typeId 0x08 (609-616)
- toBase58 (618-623)
- encode (625-630)
- getNetwork Mainnet (632-640)
- keyHashOption defined and size 28 (642-649), covered by keyHashOption == Some(AddrKeyHash(addrRoot)) plus addrRoot size 28
- hasScript, isEnterprise, scriptHashOption and hrp (651-657), only on head before
- Address.fromString (669-674)
- addrRoot size, isValid and addrType (676-687)
- derivationPath presence/absence and attributesSize (696-725); the nonempty path follows from attributesSize != 0, because attributesSize = derivationPath size (Address.scala:991-995)
- exact addrType (727-744)
The dropped checks are always true (attributesSize >= 0 at 689-694, addrType 0 or 2) or follow from toBase58 == base58 (758-775). 'different lengths' (746-756) tests only string constants. The CRC test (659-667) is kept.

findings.claim: Assertions that no main-code mutation can break, or that check too little: attributesSize >= 0 (692-694) holds for any Int size; 'Daedalus and Icarus addresses should have different lengths' (746-756) compares the lengths of two string literals in the test and calls no main code; keyHashOption is checked for size 28 only (645-647), so returning any 28-byte value passes; intercept[Exception] for addr"invalid_address" (550-552) also passes on a NullPointerException; addrType '0 or 2' (683-686) passes if the two are swapped.
findings.action: Delete 689-695 and 746-756. Compare keyHashOption with the addrRoot from parsed (or a pinned hex), intercept the specific exception type at 550-552, and assert the exact addrType (this folds into the C35-7 table).
findings.coverageRisk: none: the deleted asserts cannot fail

findings.claim: address.ArbitraryInstances is the address source for Arbitrary[TransactionOutput] (autoDerived, ledger ArbitraryInstances:335), but Arbitrary[Address] draws StakeAddress (34 %) and Network.Other (~20 % of Shelley/Stake samples, gen-stats.md), which a node cannot decode in an output (C35-1). The Byron generator writes only attribute key 2 (network magic): it never produces a derivation path (key 1), unknown attributes, or a payload over 255 bytes, so attributesSize > 0 and the 1- and 2-byte length forms in parseAttributesDirect (Address.scala:845-853) and parse (682-690) come only from the two golden vectors (697-724).
findings.action: Add genOutputAddress (Byron or Shelley, network Testnet or Mainnet) and use it for the TransactionOutput address (an explicit Arbitrary[TransactionOutput] or a given scoped to it); keep Arbitrary[Address] for address tests. Extend the Byron generator with an optional key-1 attribute of 0-300 random bytes (ByronAddress.create needs a derivationPath parameter, or build the CBOR in the generator). Prerequisite for fixing C35-1.
findings.coverageRisk: none: generator change; may surface the C35-1 mismatch in CborSerializationTest

findings.claim: Every test re-runs PBKDF2 (4096 iterations of HMAC-SHA512 for the Icarus master key) on the same mnemonic: HdAccountTest calls HdAccount.fromMnemonic(testMnemonic) with the same arguments in 17 tests and Account.createFromMnemonic(Networks.mainnet(), testMnemonic) in 6; HdKeyPairTest calls fromMnemonic/masterFromMnemonic 18 times. ledger-analysis.md: Pbkdf2.deriveKey 8.7 % and HdAccountTest 8.7 % of the module's CPU; timings: HdAccountTest 0.96 s, HdKeyPairTest 0.31 s, Bip32Ed25519Test 0.11 s.

Tests that need another passphrase or account index keep their own call.

findings.claim: About 14 tests assert only key sizes or that a pure function returns equal results twice. Sizes cannot fail: ExtendedKey requires 32-byte kL/kR/chainCode (Bip32Ed25519.scala:36-38) and VerificationKey is fixed-size, so only an exception breaks them; the 'deterministic' tests (Bip32 190-198, HdKeyPair 38-46, HdAccount 51-58) compare two calls of a function with no state. The values are pinned elsewhere: the cardano-addresses vector (Bip32Ed25519Test 50-76) and the bloxbean parity tests (HdAccountTest 169-323).

findings.verification: Bip39Test:169-181 draws one unseeded scala.util.Random entropy per size, so a failure cannot be replayed. The law isValidMnemonic(entropyToMnemonic(e)) && mnemonicToEntropy(..) == e holds for every entropy of 16/20/24/28/32 bytes (Bip39.scala:150-155 accepts exactly these sizes). Cip1852Test:95-104 tests one triple. For a, r, i in 0..Int.MaxValue, path() (Cip1852.scala:145-149) writes the decimal values, parseHardenedIndex drops the suffix and toInt parses up to 2147483647, and role/index use toInt, so parsePath(path(a,r,i)) == Some((a,r,i)) always holds. The same holds for parseAccountPath(accountPath(a)) (57-60, 187-202). scalatestplus scalacheck is a test dependency (build.sbt), and shared ledger tests already use forAll (for example PlutusScriptScopeTest).
